about: Files that fog does not compile from a dataset (typed by hand, ported from the legacy page, computed once by a script, photographs, maps, portraits). fog build explain writes a .explain beside each, with the file's own header comment and the code that uses it. Globs: * (no /), ** (any path).

files.title: The U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976, SI tables 1 and 2
files.origin: NOAA/NASA/USAF, U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NOAA-S/T 76-1562), tables as published by Public Domain Aeronautical Software (https://www.pdas.com/bigtables.html, read 2026-10-17), copied unchanged.

files.title: Aviation tab: the numbers that do not come from the flight records
files.origin: The cruise speed chosen for the level-flight figures (250 m/s at 10,668 m); the two aircraft of the force figure; three airports for the heading indicators; EI-GJT (Boeing 737-800, 9 October 2018): its inertial ground speed read by eye off figure 3 of AAIB Bulletin 12/2019 (a PDF), and its track off figure 4; One More Orbit (Gulfstream G650ER, 9-11 July 2019): times from the FAI record and the mission's site; the airports' short names are ours.
files.license: other: facts with their sources (each in the file)
files.caveats: The EI-GJT speeds are read off a printed figure, about ±2 % on each point; the start and heading of its track are decoration, not data.

files.title: Celestial theodolite: every complete case of the project's data table
files.made_by: ported verbatim from legacy/flat-or-globe-2.20.0.html (CT_PEAKS, CT_LATS, CT_CASES)
files.origin: The data_table of the Celestial Theodolite project (heights, distance, geometric and apparent star altitudes at both ends), as the legacy page typed it; nothing fitted.
files.license: other: the project's published table, cited in the ct tab
files.caveats: Typed by hand in the legacy page; the ct tab recomputes every case from these seven numbers, which shows a mistyped one as an outlier.

files.title: Horizon curvature: the documented cases of Lynch (2008)
files.origin: D. K. Lynch, Visually discerning the curvature of the Earth, Applied Optics 47(34) (2008) H39-H43; heights given in feet there, converted (1 ft = 0.3048 m).
files.license: other: facts from a cited article

files.title: Horizon dip: documented viewpoints
files.made_by: ported verbatim from the legacy page (DIP_SPOTS, VANTAGE)
files.origin: Published heights of each viewpoint (summits, towers, aircraft cruise levels), as typed by the legacy page.

files.title: Elevation angles: documented sightlines and the photographs measured
files.made_by: ported verbatim from the legacy page (PRESETS), then extended by hand
files.origin: Published summit heights and positions for each sightline; the photographs (public/photos/elev-*.jpg) and their camera fits come from research/align_photo.py and research/fit_camera_caussols.py.

files.title: The cases of the 'flatten the Earth' figure
files.origin: One case per tab, taken from the cases that tab already cites (dip, hh, elev).

files.title: Hidden height: documented sightlines, cases and records
files.made_by: ported verbatim from the legacy page (HH_PRESETS, HH_CASES, HH_RECORDS)
files.origin: Published heights and distances of each sightline or record, with its source in the hh tab.

files.title: Observation guide: the viewpoint and its targets
files.made_by: ported verbatim from the legacy page
files.origin: Positions and heights of the 'Globe spot' viewpoint and of four summits (maps and published heights; Mourre Frey located in the terrain model at its published bearing and distance, flagged); distances and azimuths computed by great circle.
files.caveats: The distances come from coordinates on a sphere: the radius enters there (a check, rule 10).

files.title: Rotation: ring lasers and falling bodies, as published
files.origin: Stedman, Hurst & Schreiber 2007 (arXiv:0707.1377) tables 1 and 2, Schreiber et al. 2004 (arXiv:physics/0406156), and the falling-body experiments named in the file.

files.title: Global Seismographic Network stations used as observation sites
files.made_by: ported verbatim from the legacy page (SEIS_STATIONS)
files.origin: Nominal positions of GSN stations (EarthScope / NSF SAGE), rounded to 0.01 degree.

files.title: Surveying: levelling cases, triangles, zenith lines
files.made_by: ported verbatim from the legacy page (SURV_LVL, SURV_TRI, SV_ZEN, SV_TRI)
files.origin: Seven NGS lines of 1977 and 25 lines of the 1900 transcontinental triangulation as transcribed by W. Bislin, and documented levelling cases.

files.title: Reciprocal zenith angles and EDM distances (Kozlowski)
files.origin: J. Kozlowski, Zenith Angle Projects (4-page PDF hosted by W. Bislin, 2004-04): the EDM slope distances measured by the instrument (the DELTA XYZ chords, which saw the ellipsoid, are not kept).
files.license: other: facts from a cited document

files.title: GPS constellation constants

files.origin: Published semi-major axis and inclination of the GPS orbits (sources [1]-[3] of the gps tab).

files.title: Coastlines of the flat-map panels
files.origin: Natural Earth 1:110m, simplified (Douglas-Peucker 0.55 degree), quantised to 0.1 degree, delta-encoded.

files.title: 49 bright stars (Yale Bright Star Catalogue)

files.title: The sea-horizon dip measured on the Caussols photograph (13 June 2026)
files.origin: The photograph data/elev/caussols-2026-06-13-original.jpg by Xyphophor (https://x.com/Xyphophor), the site's author: camera fitted (EXIF focal length, heading, tilt, roll) on the two near summits, then the horizon's altitude; the tab recomputes R from the dip.

files.title: Bordighera seen from a balcony near Antibes: the buildings and the hills
files.origin: IGN LiDAR HD (the eye's ground), OpenStreetMap building footprints (ODbL), Copernicus DSM and TINITALY 1.1 (INGV, CC BY 4.0) for heights; the eye's position is private (data/hh/bordighera/raw/eye.json, never in git).
files.license: ODbL-1.0 for the buildings (derived from OpenStreetMap); CC-BY-4.0 for the rest
files.caveats: Positions are given relative to the eye, to the metre; the eye itself is not published.

files.title: The Bordighera photograph DSCN7496 placed on the hh scene
files.origin: The photograph by Xyphophor (https://x.com/Xyphophor), the site's author (Nikon P900, 28 March 2026, 17:34), its scale from the EXIF, levelled on its sea horizon; the azimuth is its only free parameter.

files.title: Magnetism: the flat models' free parameters fitted to the measured dips
files.origin: Least squares on the inclination only, over src/data/presets/mag-obs.js (fog build mag-obs).

files.title: Aviation: the best layout of the airports on a plane
files.origin: Fitted to the measured flight times of src/data/presets/avia-flights.js (fog build avia-flights).

files.title: Horizon profiles of the viewpoints (plane, straight-ray globe, refracted globe)
files.origin: Terrain read along each azimuth from IGN LiDAR HD (France, Licence Ouverte), Copernicus GLO-30 (outside France) and the BEV ALS terrain model (Austria, CC BY 4.0); three curves from one reading of the terrain.
files.license: CC-BY-4.0 (derived from the terrain models named)
files.caveats: Distances along the ground come from the terrain models' coordinates: the radius enters there (a check, rule 10).

files.title: Horizon profile of the 'Globe spot' viewpoint (obs tab)
files.origin: IGN LiDAR HD terrain (about 1 m); three curves from one reading of the terrain.
files.license: CC-BY-4.0 (derived from IGN LiDAR HD, Licence Ouverte)
